record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: In what sense does a Regge spacetime, described as a piecewise linear manifold with a piecewise linear metric given by edge lengths, approximate a smooth vacuum spacetime, and how should analogous convergence questions be formulated for numerical relativity spacetimes?

evidence.quote: In what sense does a Regge spacetime [RT],[BrL] - a piecewise linear (PL) manifold with PL metric (=leglengths) - approximate a smooth vacuum spacetime? A similar question applies to the spacetimes constructed by numerical relativity.

artifact.category_tag: Regge calculus and numerical relativity convergence
artifact.status_search_result: Partial results exist: Barrett analyzed linearized convergence of Regge calculus to continuum Einstein equations; recent work (e.g., on the definition of curvature in Regge calculus, IMA J. Numer. Anal. 2024) shows that smoothed PL metrics yield densitized scalar curvatures converging in the sense of measures to the Regge curvature, and the Regge action converges to the continuum Einstein-Hilbert action under fatness conditions on simplices. However, a fully general theorem establishing convergence of vacuum Regge spacetimes to smooth vacuum Einstein solutions, and rigorous convergence theorems for general numerical-relativity evolutions, remain open in full generality.

status_evidence.title: On the definition of curvature in Regge calculus
status_evidence.snippet: Smoothed PL metrics have densitized scalar curvature converging, in the sense of measures, to the Regge curvature as the smoothing parameter tends to zero.
status_evidence.claim: Recent rigorous result on convergence of curvature in Regge calculus, but only partial.

status_evidence.title: On the linearization of Regge calculus
status_evidence.snippet: Barrett studied the relationship between Regge solutions and continuum Einstein solutions and formulated a convergence criterion in the linearized case.
status_evidence.claim: Linearized convergence has been addressed; nonlinear convergence to vacuum Einstein remains incomplete.
